title: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
source_used: Reuters text as carried by The Economic Times (the Reuters page returned 401)
key_facts: Amazon confirmed on Friday (9 Oct) that it is shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after announcing its first tablets featuring the voice assistant.
Daniel Rausch, a 17-year Amazon veteran and vice president of Alexa and Echo for over three years, is stepping away from the unit next month.
He will return in another capacity in the devices and services division in 2027.
Aidan Marcuss, vice president of Fire TV, advertising and the Amazon appstore, who joined from Microsoft in early 2025, replaces him.
Kevin Keith keeps his product and marketing role and takes on Marcuss' responsibilities for now.
Amazon declined to give more detail; Alexa has been a consistent money-loser since 2014, per Reuters.
Alexa+, the generative-AI version, is in the new Alexa Tablets and is included in the $139-per-year Prime membership or $20 a month standalone.
quote_evidence: Amazon on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its first tablet computers featuring the voice assistant.
The company declined to provide additional detail about the changes.
why_it_matters_hint: Leadership of Amazon's money-losing voice assistant changes as its generative-AI version launches on tablets.
